correctness.rationale: Every even endomorphism is diagonal because the two homogeneous components are one-dimensional. The Rota–Baxter identity reduces to a(a+lambda)=0, b(b+lambda)=0, and b^2=a(2b+lambda); the Nijenhuis identity reduces to (a-b)^2=0; the alpha^k-centroid reduces to b=(-1)^k a; and the averaging equations reduce to b(a-b)=0, b((-1)^k a-b)=0, and ab(((-1)^k)-1)=0. These reductions prove the stated loci over every field of characteristic different from two. The bundled checker independently replays all even operators over four odd prime fields.

value.rationale: The example is not an arbitrary slice: the primary source introduces it specifically to exhibit a Rota–Baxter Hom-associative color algebra, and a later paper reuses the same object and operator as a construction seed. Showing that the displayed Rota–Baxter operator is the unique nonzero branch, while Nijenhuis and centroid operators are rigid and averaging operators alone split by exponent parity, gives a complete structural inventory for an actual literature example and identifies a precise parity phenomenon that is invisible from the isolated example.
